html:
The Bitterroot Salish, long called the Flathead, are an Interior Salish people of western Montana. Their home was the Bitterroot Valley and the mountain valleys west of the Continental Divide. The name Flathead is a misnomer: they never shaped their heads.

They fished, dug camas and bitterroot, and hunted. After they got horses in the early 1700s they rode east across the Rockies each year to hunt bison, which brought them into long wars with the Blackfoot.

In 1805 they welcomed the Lewis and Clark Expedition at Ross's Hole and traded them horses. In 1831 they sent men to St. Louis asking for "Black Robes", and the Jesuit Pierre-Jean De Smet founded St. Mary's Mission among them in 1841.

The Hellgate Treaty of 1855 created the Flathead Reservation to the north, and in 1891 the last band was forced out of the Bitterroot. They now form part of the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes with the Pend d'Oreille and Kootenai.
